title: From alert to action: page on failed pipeline runs, then fix the cause
skills: lab alerts replay: reading when a rule fires and resolves
acting on the cause, not the symptom

ticket.subject: The finance loads failed all night and we found out at 07:30
body: Our finance pipelines in the data factory `adf-finance-prod` (resource group `rg-finance-prod`) run every
15 minutes. Since sometime last night every run fails, and nobody was told. Two things, in this order:
1. **An alert that pages.** A metric alert `adf-finance-failed-runs` on the factory's `PipelineFailedRuns`:
the **total** over a **5-minute** window, evaluated **every minute**, above 0. Severity **1** (Error: the
month-end close depends on these loads), notifying the action group `ag-finance-oncall`.
2. **Read what it would have done last night**: replay the night against it (`lab alerts replay`) and write
in `incident.txt` the time (UTC) of the first page. Then find the cause (the factory runs its copies
through a self-hosted integration runtime on a VM of the same resource group), fix it, and write the
cause and your action in the note.
This is the lab's simulated subscription: the metrics are a recorded scenario and nothing is sent to Azure.

acceptance.text: A rule on PipelineFailedRuns of adf-finance-prod pages ag-finance-oncall (sev 0-1) within two minutes of the first failure, and never before it.

checks.fail: The alert would not have paged as the ticket asks:

acceptance.text: You replayed the night after the last change to your rule, and the note gives the first page at 03:16 UTC.

checks.fail: The rule was not replayed after its last change.
incident.txt does not give the time of the first page the replay shows.

acceptance.text: The cause (vm-shir-finance, deallocated) is in the note, and the VM was started again.

checks.fail: incident.txt does not name the cause.

checks.name: vm-shir-finance
checks.fail: The integration runtime's VM is still not running.
The VMs were not looked at before acting.

hints: `az monitor metrics list-definitions --resource adf-finance-prod` lists the factory's metrics; `az monitor action-group list -o table` the action groups.
The condition is one string: `--condition "total PipelineFailedRuns > 0"`; then `--window-size 5m --evaluation-frequency 1m --severity 1 --action ag-finance-oncall`.
Severity goes from 0 (Critical) to 4 (Verbose): a smaller number is more urgent. An alert without an action group fires, but nobody hears it.

`lab alerts replay` prints, for each rule, when it fired and when it resolved over the recorded night. A rule evaluated at 03:16 looks at the five minutes before: that is when the first failure is seen.
`az vm list -g rg-finance-prod -o table` shows each VM's power state. `az vm start -g rg-finance-prod -n NAME` starts a stopped or deallocated VM.
Made a mistake in the rule? `az monitor metrics alert delete -n adf-finance-failed-runs -g rg-finance-prod`, create it again, and replay again.

IntegrationRuntimeAvailableNodeNumber.description: Available nodes of the self-hosted integration runtime ir-finance

Percentage CPU.description: The percentage of allocated compute units in use by the VM

VmAvailabilityMetric.description: 1 while the VM is up, 0 while it is not available

reference.infra: az monitor metrics alert create -n adf-finance-failed-runs -g rg-finance-prod --scopes adf-finance-prod --condition "total PipelineFailedRuns > 0" --window-size 5m --evaluation-frequency 1m --severity 1 --action ag-finance-oncall --description "A finance pipeline run failed"
az monitor metrics list --resource vm-shir-finance --metric VmAvailabilityMetric --interval 15m --start-time 2026-10-12T02:30:00Z --end-time 2026-10-12T04:00:00Z
